name: py-interval-set
instruction: Implement interval_set.py with three functions over HALF-OPEN integer intervals [start, end): normalize(intervals) -> list, union(a, b) -> list, difference(a, b) -> list. A normalized list is sorted by start, contains no empty interval (start >= end is dropped), and has no overlapping OR ADJACENT intervals - [0,5) and [5,9) merge into [0,9). union merges both inputs; difference removes every point of b from a, which can SPLIT an interval of a into two. All three return normalized lists of (start, end) tuples and must not mutate their arguments. An interval whose start or end is not an int raises ValueError.
gateCmd:
python3 - <<'GATEPY'
from interval_set import normalize
assert normalize([(0, 5), (5, 9)]) == [(0, 9)], normalize([(0, 5), (5, 9)])
print('gate ok')
GATEPY
verifyCmd:
python3 - <<'VERIFYPY'
from interval_set import normalize, union, difference

def chk(got, want, m):
    assert got == want, '%s: %r want %r' % (m, got, want)

chk(normalize([]), [], 'empty')
chk(normalize([(0, 5)]), [(0, 5)], 'single')
chk(normalize([(5, 9), (0, 3)]), [(0, 3), (5, 9)], 'sorted')
chk(normalize([(0, 5), (5, 9)]), [(0, 9)], 'adjacent merge')
chk(normalize([(0, 5), (3, 9)]), [(0, 9)], 'overlap merge')
chk(normalize([(0, 9), (3, 5)]), [(0, 9)], 'contained')
chk(normalize([(3, 3)]), [], 'empty interval dropped')
chk(normalize([(5, 1)]), [], 'inverted dropped')
chk(normalize([(0, 1), (2, 3), (1, 2)]), [(0, 3)], 'chain merges')

chk(union([(0, 3)], [(5, 9)]), [(0, 3), (5, 9)], 'disjoint union')
chk(union([(0, 5)], [(3, 9)]), [(0, 9)], 'overlapping union')
chk(union([], [(1, 2)]), [(1, 2)], 'union with empty')

chk(difference([(0, 10)], [(3, 5)]), [(0, 3), (5, 10)], 'difference splits')
chk(difference([(0, 10)], [(0, 10)]), [], 'difference all')
chk(difference([(0, 10)], []), [(0, 10)], 'difference nothing')
chk(difference([(0, 10)], [(0, 3)]), [(3, 10)], 'trim front')
chk(difference([(0, 10)], [(7, 20)]), [(0, 7)], 'trim back')
chk(difference([(0, 10)], [(2, 4), (6, 8)]), [(0, 2), (4, 6), (8, 10)], 'multiple holes')
chk(difference([(0, 5), (10, 15)], [(3, 12)]), [(0, 3), (12, 15)], 'across intervals')
chk(difference([(0, 5)], [(5, 9)]), [(0, 5)], 'adjacent does not cut')

# Must not mutate inputs.
a = [(0, 10)]
b = [(3, 5)]
difference(a, b); union(a, b); normalize(a)
chk(a, [(0, 10)], 'a unmutated')
chk(b, [(3, 5)], 'b unmutated')

# Membership cross-check against a brute-force point set.
def points(ivs):
    out = set()
    for s, e in ivs:
        out.update(range(s, e))
    return out

A = [(0, 7), (10, 14), (20, 22)]
B = [(3, 11), (13, 21)]
assert points(union(A, B)) == points(A) | points(B), 'union point set'
assert points(difference(A, B)) == points(A) - points(B), 'difference point set'

for bad in [[(0, 'x')], [('a', 5)], [(1.5, 3)]]:
    try:
        normalize(bad)
        raise SystemExit('no ValueError for %r' % (bad,))
    except ValueError:
        pass
print('ok')
VERIFYPY
